chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: With whomever you intermingle, if you are able to ensure that your hand is the upper one over them, then do so.

key_terms.اليد العليا: The upper hand — a classical Arabic metaphor for the giver's position, opposite of the lower hand (the receiver)
key_terms.فافعل: Then do so — an imperative urging positive action when capability exists

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the upper hand in social relations?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) taught that in social dealings, one should strive to be in the position of the giver rather than the receiver. The expression 'the upper hand' (al-yad al-'ulya) is a well-known prophetic metaphor in which giving and generosity are portrayed as superior to receiving and dependence. This teaching, transmitted through the trusted companion Muhammad ibn Muslim, encourages believers to embody generosity and self-sufficiency in all their social relationships.
